articles.title: Will developing nations be able to handle millions of AI agents?
articles.summary:
Big Tech’s newest personal agents — Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots — promise to book tables at restaurants, buy groceries, and carry out other types of digital grunt work for users.
Consumers are opting in. Muse has been downloaded 9 million times in the U.S. and Canada since its launch on September 8, market intelligence company AppMagic, told Rest of World. As many as 1.8 million people use the app daily.
Meta aspires to a global launch. “[We] are quite excited to bring personal agents to billions of people around the world,” Alexandr Wang, Meta’s chief AI officer, told the Financial Times.
Some startups are already building agents in markets that Big Tech hopes to reach. For instance, South African startup ManyHands offers Manny, a personal assistant designed to order groceries, book appointments and make payments through WhatsApp. But adapting agents to local conditions has its challenges. Anton Moulder, ManyHands’ founder, told Rest of World that getting the AI assistant to converse in all of South Africa’s 11 official spoken languages has been difficult.
Rest of World spoke to AI researchers and other experts to understand how these personal agents would perform outside Western nations.

Would AI agents understand the local language and culture?
English speakers could benefit more from AI agents, which run on top of large language models that underperform in many non-English languages.

articles.title: Musk promete dar ações da SpaceX a todas as crianças dos EUA
articles.summary:
Elon Musk prometeu dar uma ação da SpaceX a cada criança dos Estados Unidos no próximo ano. Considerando cerca de 73 milhões de menores no país e a cotação informada, a distribuição pode alcançar US$ 10,7 bilhões (aproximadamente R$ 54,1 bilhões).
O anúncio foi publicado no X um dia depois de a Anthropic revelar planos de destinar 5% de suas ações a um fundo de benefício público. Musk ainda não explicou como pretende entregar os papéis nem quem poderá recebê-los.
Doação pode ultrapassar US$ 10 bilhões
“No próximo ano, darei uma de minhas ações da SpaceX a cada criança da América”, escreveu Musk no X na segunda-feira. “Esta será a primeira de muitas.”
A promessa ainda não veio acompanhada de critérios para selecionar os beneficiários ou de informações sobre como as ações seriam transferidas.
Os papéis da SpaceX fecharam a sexta-feira cotados a US$ 146,03 (cerca de R$ 741). Segundo os dados mais recentes do Departamento do Censo dos Estados Unidos citados na reportagem original, o país tem aproximadamente 73 milhões de pessoas com menos de 18 anos.
Com uma ação para cada criança, o valor estimado seria de US$ 10,66 bilhões (cerca de R$ 54,1 bilhões).
Anthropic também anuncia iniciativa
A proposta de Musk surgiu em meio a outros compromissos de grandes empresários americanos. Um dia antes, a Anthropic anunciou que pretende destinar 5% de suas ações a um fundo de benefício público, que poderá financiar instituições de caridade ou direcionar recursos a grupos específicos da popula…

articles.title: There's always a patient zero: Defending the NetScaler front door before the patch
articles.summary:
Beyond the patch: Protecting your NetScaler gateway against future vulnerabilities
The recent disclosure of a major vulnerability in Citrix NetScaler pointed to a widespread weak point: a login page is an attack surface that can be used to compromise and access an application server. Indeed, the disclosures included an actively exploited flaw that allowed attackers to execute commands on affected gateways without signing in. As with any emergency patch, admins had to weigh cutting off or disrupting their users’ access with the risk of delaying a critical security update.
If you’re a NetScaler customer and you haven’t patched your instance, stop reading and go do that. This was a bad one. Once you’ve finished the patch, we’ll explore how to avoid a future fire drill by laying additional security controls.
This issue extends beyond NetScaler and can be applied to any internal application available on the Internet. Remote desktop portals, administrative consoles, and other publicly accessible authentication pages all deserve the same scrutiny: Does the intended audience require unrestricted Internet reachability? And can an attacker bypass this authentication check to reach the application's server?
Citrix released software updates to address the flaw, and Cloudflare followed with an emergency web application firewall (WAF) rule on October 1. But having a patch available does not guarantee safety: every instance has to be identified, updated, and tested. Applying updates across …

articles.title: The Robot I Didn’t Expect to Build
articles.summary:
The Robot I Didn’t Expect to Build
Agility Robotics’ first practical robotic worker is nothing like I dreamed
Agility Robotics, the company I cofounded out of my robotics lab at Oregon State University in 2015, has just launched Digit 5. It’s designed to be the first humanoid robot that can safely and economically do useful work at scale, allowing us to bring tens of thousands of humanoid workers into the real world. Engineered to lift 23-kilogram bins onto high shelves and with a battery that can run for 90 minutes on a 9-minute charge, Digit 5’s goal is to handle heavy warehouse tasks shift after shift, filling the need for labor in jobs that are too physically stressful or too dull for humans to want to do.
Digit 5 is what Agility has been working toward for over a decade. But the robot is heavy and bulky, lacking the graceful natural motion of its predecessors, and it’s farther than I thought possible from the robot I dreamed of building when I started this company. To deliver a useful commercial product, Agility has taken a path that is very different from what I first imagined.
From ATRIAS to Digit
My dream has always been to build robots that combine locomotion and manipulation to move through the world and interact with it as people do. I seek a mastery of motion, achieved through devices designed to navigate the constraints of physics with elegance. articles.title: Ukraine’s Starlink cutoff is a blinking red light for Canada
articles.summary:
Last Wednesday, as Russian missiles pummeled Kyiv, the Ukrainian military’s satellite communications were suddenly cut off. Ukrainian officials say the call to cut access to Starshield, Elon Musk’s military-grade Starlink product, came from the White House (allegations the US has denied). Almost simultaneously, across the Atlantic, US President Donald Trump revived his threats of Canadian annexation at a midterms rally in Arizona.
Calling Ukraine’s experience parallel to Canada’s would be disingenuous; our military does not rely on Starshield, and we are not currently at war. Our country and military do, however, rely heavily on US technology—an issue BetaKit has written about extensively. Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government has spent much of the past year pledging to change that. Carney has also promised to “diversify away from” Starlink, and has awarded a military contract to Telesat for secure Arctic satellite communications. The Department of National Defence is reportedly bringing together a suite of Canadian AI tech to build a “MAIple stack” for use in defence.
Despite a recognized need for change, the transition has been slow and uneven. Reporting from The Maple found that the DND has paid nearly $68 million to Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and their Canadian subsidiaries so far this year. articles.title: Hackers exploit SiteGuard WAF flaw to run commands as admins
articles.summary:
Hackers are exploiting an OS command-injection vulnerability in the SiteGuard Server Edition web application firewall (WAF), allowing them to execute commands with root or SYSTEM privileges on affected machines.
The security issue is tracked as CVE-2026-106931 and affects the statistics feature in host-based WAF instances, which is enabled by default.
SiteGuard is a leading Japanese WAF vendor that claims to protect more than 1.5 million websites. Based on WordPress.org statistics, the product is active on 500,000 sites.
According to the vendor’s bulletin and a warning from Japan's CERT agency, CVE-2026-106931 has critical severity and is currently being exploited in the wild.
“An OS command injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-106931) has been found in the statistics function of SiteGuard Server Edition. Abuse has already been confirmed,” reads SiteGuard’s alert.
The attacker’s identity, the victims, the scale of the attacks, and the methods used remain unclear, as neither security advisory provides these details.
According to the vendor, the following versions of the product are vulnerable to CVE-2026-106931:
- SiteGuard Server Edition for Apache httpd, Nginx, and IIS (excluding FreeBSD) versions 2.20 and later, before 8.00 Update 5.
- SiteGuard Server Edition for Apache httpd and Nginx on FreeBSD versions 2.20 and later, before 7.00 Update 6.
Successful exploitation is possible in the above versions if the statistics function is active. IIS editions 3.10 through 4.00 Update 4…

articles.title: Die Workflow-Revolution: Wie visuelles Arbeiten KI-Assets konsistent macht
articles.summary:
KI-Bilder und Videos: Die neue Methode für konsistente Ergebnisse
Die Kosten summieren sich. Wer professionelle KI-Werkzeuge nutzen will, landet monatlich schnell bei dreistelligen Abo-Beträgen. Nutzer:innen balancieren zwischen Qualitätsanspruch und der Notwendigkeit, Budget und Nerven zu schonen. Workflow-Tools nach dem Bausteinprinzip können mit diesem unübersichtlichen Prozess Schluss machen.
Visuelles Arbeiten für KI-Bilder und -Videos
In klassischen KI-Tools arbeiten Nutzer:innen meist linear: Ein Input führt zu einem Ergebnis, das sie in den nächsten Arbeitsschritt mitnehmen. Stimmt am Ende ein Detail nicht, beginnt der Prozess von vorn. Der Baustein-Ansatz aktueller Tools wie Flora oder Magnific Spaces dreht das Prinzip um: Die Arbeit lebt nicht in Chats, sondern auf einer Arbeitsfläche.
Den Anfang macht die Idee. Textbausteine auf Basis kleiner KI-Assistenten machen daraus einen verbesserten Bildprompt, und von dort führt per Drag-and-drop eine Verbindung zu einem Modul für Bildgenerierung – oder gleich zu mehreren Modulen, die unterschiedliche KI-Modelle nutzen. Den Prompt könnt ihr durch Referenzbilder als Kontext ergänzen. Jedes Bild kann in demselben Baustein neu generiert werden, ohne vorherige Versionen zu verlieren, bevor ihr im nächsten Baustein etwa Perspektive oder Beleuchtung ändert. Auch LLMs, Upscaler und andere Tools sind so ansprechbar, ebenso wie verschiedene Videomodelle, die das Standbild mit einem entsprechenden Prompt in Bewegung bringen.

articles.title: Livebox Orange, box SFR : une faille permet de pirater votre Wi-Fi sans mot de passe — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Si vous êtes chez Orange avec une Livebox 5 ou chez SFR avec une Box Plus, surveillez les annonces de votre opérateur ces prochaines semaines : c’est lui qui pousse les mises à jour de votre box internet. Le 16 octobre, à Hexacon, une conférence de sécurité informatique organisée à Paris, le chercheur belge Quentin Kaiser a présenté une faille dans le Wi-Fi de nombreuses box internet.
Il la détaille dans un long billet publié sur son site le même jour. Un pirate qui se trouve à portée du réseau peut faire exécuter ses propres commandes par la box sans connaître la clé Wi-Fi. D’après le repérage de réseaux que le chercheur a mené à Paris, ces deux modèles français (Livebox 5 et Box Plus) apparaissaient comme non corrigés au moment du relevé.
    À lire aussi : 
Box internet Orange : quel forfait Orange Livebox choisir en 2026 ?
Broadcom à l’origine de la faille
Le problème vient de Broadcom, un fabricant américain de puces. En plus des puces Wi-Fi, il fournit aux fabricants de box un kit logiciel (SDK) pour les faire fonctionner. Selon Quentin Kaiser, le code fautif se trouve dans ce kit depuis au moins 2010. Broadcom a discrètement publié une correction incomplète en 2018. Ensuite, il a conseillé aux fabricants de passer à hostapd, un autre logiciel qui gère les fonctions de point d’accès Wi-Fi. Le changement demande un gros travail d’adaptation, en particulier sur les vieilles box, et beaucoup de fabricants ne l’ont pas fait.

articles.title: 750 km d’autonomie et recharge en 20 minutes : Renault prépare une révolution pour les Scénic et Rafale électriques
articles.summary:
Renault tisse doucement mais sûrement son avenir au Mondial de l’Auto. Tout vêtu de rouge, le concept E-Space redonne de l’espoir face à un océan de SUV. Mais le futur d’une telle étude de style n’est pas encore garanti. articles.title: Anthropic destinará 5% de suas ações a fundo de benefício público
articles.summary:
A Anthropic, criadora do Claude, destinará 5% de suas ações a um fundo voltado a projetos de benefício público. A iniciativa permitirá ampliar as doações e financiar ações para enfrentar os impactos da inteligência artificial (IA) na sociedade.
O fundo poderá receber novas ações conforme a valorização da empresa. O anúncio ocorre enquanto a Anthropic planeja uma possível abertura de capital, que pode estar entre as maiores da história.
Fundo poderá receber mais ações
A estrutura prevê uma sociedade de responsabilidade limitada controlada integralmente pelo fundo. Para cada valorização de 50% da Anthropic acima de um patamar de referência ainda não divulgado, o conselho poderá autorizar a transferência de outros 2% das ações.
Os recursos poderão apoiar diferentes frentes, entre elas:
- Doações a organizações sem fins lucrativos;
- Distribuição direta de recursos a grupos específicos da população;
- Estudos sobre os efeitos da inteligência artificial no mercado de trabalho;
- Iniciativas voltadas a outras necessidades de interesse público.
A empresa informou que divulgará nos próximos meses detalhes sobre a governança do fundo, sua estrutura e os critérios para ampliar a participação acionária. Também pretende publicar um relatório sobre os avanços de sua missão de benefício público.

articles.title: Salários em tecnologia se aproximam dos R$ 40 mil; veja principais cargos • Tecnoblog
articles.summary:
Salários em tecnologia se aproximam dos R$ 40 mil; veja principais cargos
Guia Salarial 2027 da Michael Page mostra que IA é diferencial no mercado de tecnologia, mas não significa maior salário.
O Guia Salarial 2027 da Michael Page aponta um forte crescimento da inteligência artificial no mercado de tecnologia, com 33% das empresas destacando o domínio de ferramentas do tipo como um diferencial no próximo ano. Mas em termos salariais, a área não tem profissionais de IA no topo: enquanto especialistas na ferramenta têm ganhos de R$ 14 a 20 mil, gerentes recebem até R$ 37 mil em grandes empresas.
As maiores remunerações seguem com profissionais em engenharia de dados, que podem chegar a R$ 42 mil mensais. Outras áreas mais tradicionais, como ciência de dados, engenharia de software e segurança da informação, já batem os R$ 40 mil. Isso mostra que, apesar do maior espaço para IA na indústria, as áreas mais valorizadas do setor seguem sendo aquelas mais especializadas.
Além disso, a pesquisa também aponta a flexibilidade como predominante no setor, com 51% apostando no trabalho híbrido. O Tecnoblog teve acesso exclusivo ao recorte de tecnologia do levantamento, que foi realizado em 1.955 empresas, considerando 15 setores diferentes e mais de 400 cargos. Ao todo, 5.762 profissionais foram entrevistados.
O principal destaque do Guia Salarial da Michael Page é o avanço da IA no mercado de tecnologia. Aparecendo entre áreas tradicionais como ciência de dados e engenharia de software…

articles.title: Arnaques en ligne : les banques devront désormais rembourser les victimes, même en cas de négligence grave
articles.summary:
Un nouvel arrêt rendu par la Cour de justice de l’Union européenne pourrait changer la donne pour les victimes d’arnaques en ligne. En effet, il oblige les banques européennes à rembourser les personnes qui ont effectué un paiement « non autorisé », même en cas de « négligence grave ». Cet arrêt prévoit tout de même deux exceptions. Voici ce qu’il faut savoir.
Arnaques : la CJUE impose aux banques de rembourser les paiements non autorisés, même en cas de négligence grave
Ce 15 octobre 2026, la Cour de justice de l’Union européenne (CJUE) a rendu un arrêt qui va peut-être changer pas mal de choses pour les victimes d’arnaques. Concrètement, cet arrêt oblige les banques européennes à rembourser les personnes qui ont effectué un paiement « non autorisé ». L’arrêt ne mentionne pas clairement des arnaques, mais c’est bel et bien une situation à laquelle il peut s’appliquer.
Une ligne de cet arrêt est à retenir particulièrement : les banques ont l’obligation de rembourser un paiement non autorisé, même en cas de « négligence grave » de la part du client. L’arrêt l’indique clairement : « Un prestataire de services de paiement ne peut pas refuser de rembourser immédiatement à un payeur le montant d’une opération de paiement non autorisée, au motif que ce payeur aurait rendu possible cette opération par une négligence grave ». articles.title: A woman was arrested in Philly for blocking a delivery robot
articles.summary:
Carolyn Marvin was arrested and charged with disorderly conduct after blocking the path of an Uber delivery robot and refusing to get out of the way. Marvin told Philadelphia’s ABC13 “I know they’re taking the jobs of human delivery workers and so, I have been protesting them whenever I saw them by standing in front of them and preventing them from going forward.”
A woman was arrested in Philly for blocking a delivery robot
Carolyn Marvin was charged with ‘disorderly conduct’ for protesting delivery robots taking jobs.
Police responded to the scene and asked Marvin to move out of the robot’s way. When she refused, they placed her in cuffs and arrested her. The incident was captured on video and has now garnered considerable media attention.
The delivery robots have become a common sight on the streets of downtown Philadelphia and have sparked backlash. This is not even Marvin’s first brush with them. And earlier this year, one was kicked over in Center City. Broad concern has grown about how autonomous systems, including robotaxis, delivery robots, and AI agents, are impacting jobs, especially for lower-skill workers.

Toronto- and New York City-based Mecka AI, which aims to supply the training data necessary to deploy robots in the real world, has completed its second acquisition to date.
The buzzy AI startup announced today that it bought Ottawa’s Thirdspace, a popular social mobile app that Mecka described as a mix between BeReal, Instagram, and Snapchat. Thirdspace bills itself as a venue for “[in real life] side quests with friends.” The news comes shortly after Mecka revealed it had closed $60 million USD ($86 million CAD) in Series B funding from Sequoia Capital, Nvidia, Microsoft, Qualcomm, and Samsung, among others.
“They’ve captured this lightning in the bottle of what it takes to get viral.”
Launched last year by former Carleton University students Cedric Osagie and Eshan Betrabet, Thirdspace allows users to take and post photos of themselves doing fun things and invites friends to join. The images are only briefly viewable—once others have accepted the invite, they’ll get a location to join in and capture a pic together.
In an exclusive interview with BetaKit, Osagie said the goal was to build a fun, spontaneous way to encourage lonely university students to connect more in person. The idea has taken off: in less than two years, Thirdspace has amassed upwards of 20,000 downloads, 60 million views, and has been tripling its monthly active users on the back of $100,000 CAD in angel funding.

articles.title: Die Streaming-Falle: Bei diesen Anbietern müssen Sie trotz Abo mit Werbung rechnen
articles.summary:
Streaming-Falle bei Netflix, Disney, Prime & Co.: Warum du trotz Abo plötzlich Werbung siehst
Draußen ist es schon dunkel, der Herbstwind weht, es regnet. Drinnen läuft der Filmabend bei Snacks und gedimmtem Licht. Der Detektiv ist gerade dabei, den Mörder zu entlarven. „Der Täter ist …“ Schnitt. „Ralf Schumacher?!“ Das ist natürlich überspitzt dargestellt, dürfte aber für viele deutsche Streaming-Nutzer ein Stück weit zur Realität gehören. Denn laut einer Statista-Umfrage unter 4.781 Personen zwischen 18 und 64 Jahren nutzten 51 Prozent der Befragten zwischen Juni 2025 und Juni 2026 kostenlose und werbefinanzierte Streaming-Dienste, 46 Prozent zahlen für Angebote mit Werbung wie etwa Netflix.
Zwar waren mehrfache Angaben möglich und die Daten deuten laut dem Statistikdienst darauf hin, dass viele Streaming-Fans „mehrere Streamingabos abgeschlossen haben und dabei werbefinanzierte und werbefreie Angebote mischen“. (Schließlich gaben 41 Prozent an, für Angebote ohne Reklame zu zahlen.) Die Umfrage zeigt aber deutlich, dass Werbung mittlerweile für viele zum Erlebnis dazugehört.
Günstiger Einstieg ins Streaming nur mit Werbung

articles.title: Peter Lee, veterano de la investigación de Microsoft, y Ryan Roslansky, ex CEO de LinkedIn, anuncian su salida
articles.summary:
Peter Lee y Ryan Roslansky han anunciado su salida de Microsoft tras más de 16 años en la compañía y casi 18 años entre LinkedIn y Microsoft, respectivamente.
Lee había dirigido Microsoft Research y Roslansky había pasado de ser responsable de LinkedIn a encargarse también de Microsoft 365. Lee buscará nuevas oportunidades, mientras que Roslansky explicó que se marchaba por motivos familiares.
Una nueva oportunidad y un cambio de domicilio
Lee, hasta ahora presidente de Microsoft Science, comunicó su decisión en una entrada en LinkedIn, donde destacó que se trataba de “una oportunidad única en la vida”. También mencionó que el nuevo trabajo supondría un cambio sustancial con respecto a su actividad de las dos últimas décadas. Adicionalmente, afirmó que seguiría colaborando con Mayo Clinic, así como con Kaiser Permanente Bernard J. Tyson School of Medicine y con Seattle Children’s.
Lee fue profesor de informática en la Universidad Carnegie Mellon desde 1987 hasta 2010, antes de incorporarse a Microsoft. Time Magazine lo incluyó en 2024 entre las 100 personas más influyentes en salud y ciencias de la vida, según recoge su biografía en Microsoft. Además de su trayectoria profesional, Lee ha convertido coches clásicos en vehículos eléctricos. Entre ellos figuran una réplica de un Porsche 550 Spyder de 1955 y un Ford Mustang GT Fastback de 1968.

articles.title: Microsoft: October Windows Server updates break Exchange sign-in, mail flow
articles.summary:
Microsoft has confirmed that this month's Windows Server security updates are causing OWA sign-in and mail delivery issues on some Exchange Server systems.
In a new Windows release health dashboard update over the weekend, Microsoft said users may have trouble accessing email or signing in to Outlook after installing the latest updates on systems running Windows Server 2019 and later.
In some cases, affected customers are also reportedly seeing Exchange Server OWA failing with a "MapiExceptionMdbOffline: Unable to make connection to the server. (hr=0x80004005, ec=1142)" error and Event ID 1006 in the application log.

articles.title: Scale isn't one number: three ways a Kubernetes control plane runs out of room

Scale isn’t one number: three ways a Kubernetes control plane runs out of room
Three clusters in trouble, and they look nothing alike.
The first is a training fleet. It sat at a few thousand nodes for months, then a new run landed, and it’s at fifteen thousand. Kube-apiserver starts eating memory. Etcd starts complaining.
The second never passes a few thousand nodes and is having a much worse day. It’s an agent platform, and its objects are alive: sessions created, suspended, resumed, and destroyed thousands of times a minute, every transition a write.
The third is neither big nor fast: a platform cluster with two hundred operators installed and tens of thousands of objects that mostly just sit there, and every apiserver holds a copy of all of them.
Two of those are AI workloads, and one isn’t, which is the least interesting part. They’re running out of room in three different directions, and fixing one does nothing for the others.

articles.title: There’s a hidden bias affecting what we know – and don’t know – about nature
articles.summary:
Our knowledge about life on Earth is built through research on how organisms function, evolve and interact with each another and the environment. Yet there are far more species on our planet than scientists can study in detail.
So how should scientists decide which species to focus on? Fairly representing all species seems like a useful approach. It’s like predicting an election result: we can’t interview every citizen, so we need a sample that truly represents the overall population.
What drives scientists to uncover nature’s mysteries is curiosity. So, the organisms chosen for research are determined by what makes scientists most curious. And that’s causing a problem with fair representation.
In our new research, we examined research in ecology and evolution (an umbrella term for biological sciences outside biomedicine) to understand which animals are most studied and why.
Our results suggest emotion plays a bigger role in research choices than scientists usually admit.
Which animals are studied?
Our world is mostly filled with invertebrates: creatures such as bugs, spiders, worms and slugs. Vertebrates (amphibians, birds, fish, mammals and reptiles) make up only 5% of all animal species on Earth. So, if scientists want to represent animals fairly in their work, most research should be on invertebrates.
To understand how scientists’ time is spent researching the diversity of animals, we analysed almost 1.4 million scientific articles from more than 600 journals. Unsurprisin…

Vous pensiez que le MCP était le grand méchant de Tron ? Le Master Control Program du film de 1982 a désormais un homonyme nettement plus pacifique dans la tech. Du moins, pour l’instant. Le Model Context Protocol, ou MCP, est un standard qui permet aux applications utilisant un modèle d’IA d’accéder à des logiciels, des fichiers et des services en ligne. Cela concerne aussi bien un chatbot qu’un assistant intégré à un logiciel ou un agent piloté depuis un terminal, comme Claude Code ou Gemini CLI.
Pour faire simple auprès de vos proches avides de questions sur l’IA, le MCP peut permettre à une IA de consulter votre agenda ou de retrouver un document au lieu de simplement vous expliquer où cliquer. Une différence qui paraît minime sur le papier, mais qui change profondément ce qu’une IA peut faire pour nous.

Demandez à une IA de préparer votre prochaine réunion sans lui donner accès à votre agenda ni à vos documents. Elle pourra vous proposer une méthode et la décrire, mais elle n’ira guère plus loin. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.

A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. articles.title: Sony patents AI that predicts a game's next frame before the GPU finishes rendering it
articles.summary:
Forward-looking: Sony has filed a patent for an AI system that predicts a game's next frame before the graphics hardware finishes rendering it, aiming to reduce stuttering without introducing the additional latency associated with some frame-generation methods. The system uses the most recently completed frame and, optionally, recent controller input to generate a predicted frame that can be displayed while the hardware renders the next one.
The approach targets a drawback of some frame-generation techniques: they require two completed frames before generating an image to insert between them. Waiting for the second frame adds latency. Sony's system would instead use an already available frame to predict the next one, rather than waiting to interpolate between two completed frames.
That difference could help games maintain a steadier frame delivery rate when rendering slows down. However, the patent filing includes no performance measurements, leaving its effects on latency and visual quality unproven.
Sony's design uses a jointly trained encoder and decoder. The encoder converts a rendered frame into an embedding – a compact numerical representation of the image. The decoder then uses that representation to generate a predicted frame.

Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).
As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. These behaviors often lead people to describe AI as though it can think, feel, or make decisions for itself. But does behaving like a human actually convince people that a machine has consciousness?
New research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.

F5 has released out-of-band security patches to address multiple NGINX web server flaws, including three critical-severity vulnerabilities that can let attackers execute code on vulnerable systems.
The three critical vulnerabilities were found in the ngx_http_v3_module (CVE-2026-15176 and CVE-2026-97205) and the NGINX map directive (CVE-2026-93479).
Remote attackers without privileges can exploit them to launch denial-of-service (DoS) attacks or gain code execution on NGINX systems with non-default configurations.
Successful exploitation causes a heap-based buffer overflow or use-after-free in the NGINX worker process, leading to crashes or a restart. However, attackers may also be able to "execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR."
F5 released security patches for multiple NGINX software products affected by these two vulnerabilities, including NGINX Plus, NGINX Open Source, NGINX Ingress Controller, NGINX Gateway Fabric, and NGINX Instance Manager.
Security teams and admins who can't immediately install these security patches can mitigate CVE-2026-15176 by not using the 'alias' directive in a location block or the $request_filename variable, and CVE-2026-97205 by disabling asynchronous file I/O (AIO) or Server Side Includes (SSI).

Input-cost pressures intensified in the September quarter, reversing some of the moderation seen in the preceding quarter, which squeezed margins even as companies absorbed part of it to protect consumer demand during the festive season.
FMCG companies face sustained margin pressure in the second half of the current fiscal year, as rising input costs squeeze profitability, with firms weighing post-Diwali price hikes against the risk of hurting consumer demand, particularly in price-sensitive mass-market and rural categories.
Input-cost pressures intensified in the September quarter, reversing some of the moderation seen in the preceding quarter, which squeezed margins even as companies absorbed part of it to protect consumer demand during the festive season.
The increase has been uneven across commodities, with crude-linked derivatives, packaging materials, palm oil and sugar emerging as key pressure points, said Naveen Malpani, Partner and Consumer Industry Leader at Grant Thornton Bharat.
"In rupee terms, palm oil prices were approximately 21% higher year-on-year in September, while sugar prices remained around 18% higher year-on-year despite correcting 8% month-on-month," he said.
Higher costs have not been fully offset by price increases and operational efficiencies, putting pressure on operating margins, Malpani said.

articles.title: A Composable Thermal Solver For Heterogeneous 2.5D/3D-IC Packages (Cadence, Notre Dame)
articles.summary:
Researchers at Cadence Design Systems and the University of Notre Dame published “A Composable AI-Accelerated Iterative Solver for 3D-IC Thermal Modeling.”
Abstract:
“Accurate thermal analysis of heterogeneous 2.5D/3D-IC packages is essential yet computationally prohibitive. A single full-package FEM simulation can take hours, while AI-based surrogates treat the entire stack as a monolithic prediction target and must be retrained whenever the die count or topology changes. To address this limitation, this work proposes Domain-Decomposed AI-Accelerated Iterative Solver for Thermal Analysis (DAIST), a composable thermal solver that decomposes the global package simulation into block-level subdomain problems, replaces subdomain solvers with neural operators, and couples them through iterative exchanges of interfacial temperature and heat flux. This local-to-global architecture eliminates the topology lock-in of monolithic models: block-level neural operators can be directly reused in unseen package assemblies without retraining. The iterative coupling strategy further provides a controllable accuracy-runtime tradeoff, where the iteration budget can be adjusted to trade accuracy for runtime. Evaluated on a multi-chiplet system and an advanced packaging system, DAIST achieves up to 178× speedup over traditional FEM solvers with mean temperature errors of 0.068% and 0.323%, respectively, while demonstrating cross-topology reuse of block-level models across structurally distinct pac…

articles.title: Google Adopts Pyrefly for Faster, More Accurate Python Type Checking
articles.summary:
Google has replaced its long-standing Python type checker, Pytype, with Pyrefly, an open-source tool originally developed by Meta. The decision was driven by Pyrefly's advantages, including faster and more accurate type checking, and lower infrastructure costs.
As Python’s typing system evolved rapidly, Pytype faced fundamental challenges. Because it operated by analyzing compiled bytecode rather than source ASTs, keeping pace with modern typing PEPs became an increasing maintenance burden due to bytecode instability across Python releases.
According to Google’s internal benchmarks, Pyrefly is approximately 10 times faster than Pytype, reduces incremental rebuild latency by up to 98%, and cuts peak compute cost for Python type checking by more than 80%. Google also reported a 90–99% reduction in type-checking time along clean-build critical paths, substantially "eliminating a long-standing development bottleneck".
One of Pyrefly's key strengths, Google explains, is its strong conformance to Python's typing specification, passing approximately 97% of tests in the conformance suite. Pyrefly is also actively supported by the community, which helps it keep pace with new syntax, and its diagnostics provides more actionable feedback, including inline code annotations that pinpoint the root cause of errors and, in some cases, suggest fixes.
The community has responded with interest to Google's announcement. While most commenters agreed that Pytype performs worse than Pyrefly, others…

articles.title: Sangue tipo B tem mais risco de diabetes, mas hábitos pesam mais
articles.summary:
Uma revisão científica publicada em 2024 identificou uma associação entre o sangue tipo B e o risco de desenvolver diabetes tipo 2. O resultado surgiu de uma análise abrangente de estudos sobre grupos sanguíneos e saúde, que avaliou centenas de possíveis relações com diferentes doenças.
A pesquisa apontou que pessoas com sangue B positivo ou negativo apresentam, em média, risco 28% maior de desenvolver a doença do que indivíduos com outros tipos sanguíneos. Os autores, porém, ressaltam que essa relação não explica a causa do diabetes nem permite prever quem terá a condição.
Apenas uma associação apresentou evidências convincentes
Liderada pela epidemiologista Fang-Hua Liu, do Hospital Shengjing da Universidade Médica da China, a equipe analisou 51 revisões científicas que, juntas, investigaram 270 possíveis relações entre tipos sanguíneos e problemas de saúde.
Essas revisões reúnem resultados de pesquisas anteriores para identificar padrões que talvez não apareçam em um único estudo. Os pesquisadores, então, verificaram se as conclusões eram consistentes, se havia participantes suficientes nas pesquisas e se os resultados poderiam ter sido influenciados por falhas ou distorções. Também avaliaram a possibilidade de que as associações desaparecessem em estudos futuros.

articles.title: MITRE ATT&CK v20 Catalogs AI Abuse, MFA Bypass, Water Utility Attacks
articles.summary:
MITRE last week released version 20 of its ATT&CK framework, adding entries that cover AI abuse, MFA bypass, and recent attacks on water utilities.
The organization says the biggest change in ATT&CK v20 is “expanded coverage of recent adversary activity and tradecraft.”
The Enterprise domain gets nine additions, counting both techniques and sub-techniques. Prompt injection is now tracked as two techniques, one for malicious instructions typed straight into an LLM’s interface and one for instructions hidden in material the model ingests.
Another technique describes attackers using an organization’s own AI agents to steal data. Sub-techniques also cover poisoning web content to sway AI search and assistant recommendations, and disrupting LLM-assisted analysis of malware.
Separately, a new technique tracks the theft of application-specific passwords, which attackers can use to sign in without an MFA prompt. Another addresses bypassing CAPTCHA checks, with sub-techniques for automatically solving them and for avoiding them.
The sub-technique for compromised software dependencies and development tools now also covers IDE and coding agent configuration files. MITRE says the additions help capture “how adversaries get around Multi-Factor Authentication, bot checks, and AI systems.”

articles.title: La UCO arresta a un adolescente de 16 años como presunto líder de KillSec, responsable de mil ciberataques
articles.summary:
Los investigadores del Departamento de Cibercrimen de la Unidad Central Operativa (UCO) de la Guardia Civil han identificado a un chico rumano de 16 años, que vive en la provincia de Alicante, como presunto administrador del grupo de ransomware KillSec tras analizar una imagen de perfil.
Según los investigadores, sus miembros habrían llevado a cabo más de 1.000 ataques cibernéticos en todo el mundo, de los cuales unos 500 habrían tenido éxito, contra más de 280 víctimas.
Algunas de ellas habrían pagado rescates de alrededor de 500.000 euros en criptomonedas. Durante los registros en una vivienda y en la oficina de un hotel de la provincia, los agentes intervinieron ordenadores, teléfonos móviles y carteras de criptoactivos, y una mujer quedó como investigada por su presunta relación con los hechos.
¿Cómo se llegó hasta un chaval de 16 años?
La Operación Rotoma se inició en 2025 a partir de la colaboración con la oficina del FBI en San Juan de Puerto Rico, que buscaba a personas relacionadas con KillSec que pudieran residir en España.
Por otro lado, los Mossos d’Esquadra habían abierto una investigación por un ataque contra la entidad pública catalana Infraestructures.cat a principios de 2025: los delincuentes accedieron a sus sistemas, sustrajeron información sensible e intentaron extorsionarla, con daños estimados en cerca de un millón de euros. La entidad asegura que no pagó ningún rescate.

articles.title: Inside the Underground Market for Know Your Client Services
articles.summary:
In February 2026, the operator of OnlyFake pleaded guilty in the United States for his role in a service that generated more than 10,000 fraudulent digital identity documents. Customers could create passports, driver’s licenses, Social Security cards, and documents from dozens of countries, then choose whether each appeared as a scan or a photograph of a physical ID.
According to the U.S. Department of Justice, the documents allowed cybercriminals to conceal their identities, circumvent identity checks at banks and cryptocurrency exchanges, and launder money.
The activity extends beyond fabricated documents. In underground communities monitored by Flare's platform, actors advertise manipulated photographs and videos, assistance with live identity verification, and accounts they claim have already passed identity checks.
Each year, Flare collects hundreds of thousands of search results related to Know Your Client (KYC) services and the trade in verified accounts. Activity observed between March and September 2026 shows how these offerings are packaged and promoted across underground markets.
What is KYC?
It is the process that financial institutions use to establish a customer’s identity and assess the risk of providing services to them.

articles.title: N'achetez pas de smartphone sur Leboncoin, Vinted ou eBay après le 17 octobre

Un vêtement dérobé peut facilement changer de mains sans que son propriétaire puisse le retrouver. Pour un smartphone, c’est une autre histoire : plusieurs dispositifs permettent de bloquer son utilisation, en coupant son accès aux réseaux mobiles ou en verrouillant directement l’appareil.
Les opérateurs peuvent bloquer un téléphone grâce à son IMEI, un identifiant à 15 chiffres. Changer de carte SIM ne suffit donc pas à retrouver du réseau : c’est le téléphone lui-même qui est visé. articles.title: ‘Fortnite’ al fin llegará a Linux: ¿Por qué ha tardado tanto?
articles.summary:
Puede que Fortnite ya no sea el fenómeno de hace unos años, pero eso no quiere decir que no siga siendo un juego tremendamente popular en todo el mundo. Y en el futuro cercano va a expandir su base de usuarios de la mano de una versión oficial para distribuciones Linux. Así lo anunció la propia Epic Games días atrás al presentar la nueva versión de su Launcher para ordenadores.
La gran pregunta es por qué la compañía se ha demorado tanto en preparar una versión de Fortnite para Linux. Muchas empresas no llevan sus juegos a Linux argumentando que las medidas antitrampas que existen en la actualidad no son suficientes para que la experiencia sea justa para todos los usuarios.

Plus que quelques mois. La France, comme une grande partie des États membres de l’Union européenne, n’a plus que quelques mois pour mettre en place la réforme votée le 21 octobre 2025. Celle-ci instaure une nécessité de renouveler son permis de conduire tous les 15 ans. Adoptée à 339 voix pour et 240 voix contre, la directive (UE) 2025/2205 datée du 22 octobre 2025 signe la fin du permis à vie dans les États qui le proposent, France en tête.
Le délai légal pour la mise en place de cette directive est fixé à trois ans après la signature. Concrètement, cela revient à dire que la mesure doit être appliquée en France avant le 21 octobre 2028. Il reste moins de deux ans au gouvernement pour engager ce changement. La France n’est d’ailleurs pas la seule à prendre son temps : ils ne seraient que cinq États, sur les vingt-deux à avoir officiellement franchi le pas (Italie, Danemark, Pays-Bas, Finlande et Portugal).
Que prévoit le texte ?
Le texte européen voté l’an dernier prévoit qu’un contrôle médical doit être effectué tous les quinze ans afin de renouveler la validité du permis de conduire pour une nouvelle période de quinze ans. C’est un cadre légal minimum, c’est-à-dire que chaque État membre est libre de durcir les règles.

articles.title: One pilot, two aircraft: F-22 Raptor directs autonomous combat drone in glimpse of future air warfare
articles.summary:
What just happened? The US Air Force has announced the military's latest move toward an autonomous future. This time, an F-22 Raptor pilot directed a drone during simulated combat. The pilot issued high-level tactical directives to the YFQ-44A while flying, essentially turning it into an unpiloted wingman.
The demonstration took place earlier this month, when the Raptor and Anduril's YFQ-44A Fury took off from Edwards Air Force Base in California.
Once airborne, the pilot sent an updated mission plan over a tactical data link. The drone's onboard software interpreted those instructions and carried out the maneuvers and simulated combat tasks.
While it might sound like it, this wasn't a case of someone flying two aircraft at once. The pilot decided what the Fury should do, while the autonomous system handled the flight controls.
The test was part of the Collaborative Combat Aircraft program. The initiative's aim is to field low-cost, semi-autonomous uncrewed aerial vehicles that fly alongside crewed fifth- and sixth-generation fighter jets.
The test involved just one Raptor and one Fury, but the longer-term ambition is for a single pilot to direct several autonomous wingmen. Those aircraft could bring extra weapons, sensors, and electronic warfare equipment to a mission.

articles.title: From Macro to Micro, and Back - EE Times
articles.summary:
Looking at this year’s Nobel prizes, I was struck by how many of them explain the behavior of a large system through its smallest parts.
Four different Nobel prizes, one common theme
The medicine prize went to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, and Georg Nagel for optogenetics. Hegemann and Nagel found that a protein from green algae could make cells respond to light, and Deisseroth put its gene into neurons, so researchers can switch specific brain cells on and off with a flash of light. For the first time, neuroscientists could test what an individual neuron does and how groups of neurons produce memories, feelings, and behavior.
The chemistry prize went to Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai for their work on chirality, the property of molecules that come in two mirror-image forms, like our left and right hands. Living organisms use only one form of each, and the long-standing puzzle was how that happened. Soai found a reaction in which a minuscule imbalance between the two forms amplifies itself, which the Nobel Committee described as the first time anyone had created chirality from non-chiral molecules since the dawn of life. It is a striking example of micro shaping macro, since a tiny imbalance between individual molecules, amplified by feedback, ended up determining a property of all life on Earth.

No more half-hour recharges, ideal for safety and rescue.
DJI has delivered a battery-swapping drone dock, the Dock 4, with an automated 25-second swap this week, according to a company press release. The company emphasizes the safety angle, pitching the Dock 4 as a “dock-as-a-first-responder (DFR)” solution. Its product page calls it “Always There, Always Ready.” Swapping the battery takes less than half a minute, and the drone is back in the air within 45 seconds of landing. The dock also charges two 925 g battery packs, rated at 260 Wh for 400 cycles, at once, estimated to take 27 minutes to get each from 15% to 95%.
The packs also double as backup power, rated at about 4.5 hours each, in sequence. Additionally, with at least two packs loaded, the dock is able to continue swapping even when grid power is lost, although backup power doesn’t charge the packs. articles.title: NestJS 12: ESM Packages, Standard Schema Validation and Native Observability
articles.summary:
NestJS, the TypeScript framework for building server-side Node.js applications, has released version 12, a major release that moves its core packages to ESM, adds first-class Standard Schema validation, rebuilds the CLI and introduces an official observability SDK. It follows April's roadmap, and creator Kamil Myśliwiec's announcement on X has passed 1,100 likes and 66,000 views.
The ESM change is the headline, largely because it asks so little of existing teams. Core packages now ship as ESM, but CommonJS applications keep working through Node.js require(esm) support, which is why v12 requires Node.js 20.19+ or 22.12+. nest new now asks whether to generate a CJS or ESM project, with ESM projects defaulting to Vitest and oxlint, while Rspack replaces webpack as the monorepo bundler. Developer Anton Chapala's preview benchmarks found no meaningful startup or memory gains from ESM, concluding it "is a massive cleanup of tooling and configuration debt" rather than a performance upgrade.
Day-to-day ergonomics change most around validation. Route decorators such as @Body(), @Query() and @Param() accept a schema option taking any Standard Schema compatible object, so Zod, Valibot and ArkType work without third-party wrappers once the new pipe is registered.
class-validator remains the documented default. Blogger iiaku argued that building on a spec rather than on Zod directly "keeps the choice in my hands while removing the boilerplate", though a commenter on ByteIota's preview cov…

Una comida, dos personas. Antes de que llegue la primera ración, uno de los comensales gira su teléfono y lo deja sobre el mantel con la pantalla hacia abajo. Hay quien lo interpreta como desconfianza, pero la explicación es otra: quiere librarse de las notificaciones y las llamadas entrantes y de la presión constante de estar disponible en todo momento. Al fin y al cabo, es solo una interpretación, y no se apoya en ningún experimento científico que estudie sus motivaciones.
Lo que sí han estudiado los experimentos es el efecto de tener el móvil a la vista.
En la Universidad de Essex, Andrew Przybylski y Netta Weinstein realizaron un experimento con parejas de desconocidos que hablaban entre ellos durante diez minutos con un teléfono o un cuaderno sobre una mesa cercana.
En su trabajo, publicado en el Journal of Social and Personal Relationships, el teléfono se asoció con una menor cercanía y una conversación de menor calidad y, en un segundo experimento, con una menor confianza y empatía, aunque solo cuando hablaban de algo personal: con un tema trivial no hubo diferencias. Después, otro grupo de científicos, ya fuera del Reino Unido, llevó la comparación a conversaciones reales.
Shalini Misra, de Virginia Tech, observó 100 conversaciones reales entre dos personas en entornos informales. Aquellas que tuvieron lugar sin ningún dispositivo a la vista salieron mejor valoradas. “En presencia de un dispositivo móvil hay menos contacto visual”, resumía la investigadora.

articles.title: Exploited Fortinet Bug Linked to Stealthy FortiGate Implant in Telecom Hack
articles.summary:
A suspected state-sponsored threat actor exploited multiple Fortinet vulnerabilities in an attack against a telecommunications organization, Palo Alto Networks reports.
The intrusion, attributed to UNC5820 (tracked by Palo Alto Networks as CL-STA-0954), occurred in September 2024 and resulted in long-term access to the victim’s environment.
Initial access was obtained through the exploitation of a critical remote code execution (RCE) bug in FortiManager, tracked as CVE-2024-47575 and patched in October 2024 as a zero-day.
Shortly after the patches were rolled out, Mandiant warned that UNC5820 had been exploiting the flaw, named FortiJump, since at least June 2024.
A fresh report from Palo Alto Networks shows that UNC5820 also exploited CVE-2025-61624, a path traversal vulnerability affecting multiple Fortinet products, as part of the same intrusion.
Impacting FortiOS, FortiPAM, FortiProxy, and FortiSwitchManager and patched in April 2026, the security defect could allow authenticated attackers to write or delete arbitrary files. Fortinet flagged its exploitation as a zero-day at the time of disclosure.
On Friday, the US cybersecurity agency CISA added CVE-2025-61624 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) list, urging federal agencies to patch it immediately.
UNC5820 appears to have exploited the path traversal as a zero-day to deploy a previously unknown FortiGate implant dubbed PeerStitch.

articles.title: Pourquoi votre Wi-Fi rame toujours alors que vous êtes passé à la fibre optique
articles.summary:
Cette confusion très courante qui vous fait croire que votre connexion fibre est lente
Vous venez de passer à la fibre optique mais votre connexion sans fil rame toujours autant sur votre smartphone ou ordinateur ? C’est normal, car fibre et Wi-Fi sont deux choses bien différentes.
Souscrire à une offre fibre promettant un débit très élevé donne souvent l’illusion que tous les problèmes de connexion appartiennent au passé. Pourtant, la déception est fréquente une fois la nouvelle box Internet installée : vidéos qui saccadent, téléchargements lents, lags dans vos jeux vidéo favoris... Cette frustration repose sur une confusion très courante entre la puissance qui arrive jusqu’à votre box, sa diffusion dans votre logement, puis sa réception sur vos appareils.
La différence fondamentale entre la fibre et le réseau sans fil
Pour bien comprendre le problème, il faut dissocier deux technologies totalement indépendantes. La fibre optique agit comme une immense autoroute capable de transporter une quantité colossale de données à vitesse grand V, mais cette prouesse s’arrête pile à l’arrière de votre box Internet. Microsoft has released .NET 11 Release Candidate 2 with a go-live license for production use, as stated in the announcement. The build is supported in Visual Studio 2026 Insiders and in Visual Studio Code with the C# Dev Kit. As reported, it brings changes across the libraries, runtime, SDK, NuGet, F#, ASP.NET Core, .NET MAUI, and Windows Forms, with no new C# language features.
In the libraries, CborReader can now read a payload delivered in chunks, using isFinalBlock and SlideData, in Lax conformance mode only. Two experimental cryptography types arrive: CompositeMLKem combines post-quantum and classical key encapsulation, and Hpke provides Hybrid Public Key Encryption with classical DHKEM suites only.
Both require opting in through SYSLIB5009 and SYSLIB5006, as described in the release notes. ValidationAttribute.FormatMessage lets a host supply a message template for the attribute to fill in, and SocketsHttpHandler.InitialHttp2MaxConcurrentStreams caps streams on a new HTTP/2 connection until the server's SETTINGS frame arrives.
The runtime release focuses on reliability but carries one breaking change. CoreCLR now disables advisory file locking by default on iOS and tvOS, because, as stated, FileStream lock in RC 1 could cause the OS to terminate an app entering the background. FileShare restrictions are no longer enforced there, and setting DOTNET_SYSTEM_IO_DISABLEFILELOCKING to 0 restores locking, according to the release.

Personal information on current and former California public school students was copied from a file transfer system belonging to Educational Testing Service (ETS), according to the California Department of Education (CDE).
ETS is a nonprofit that handles state and federally mandated testing under a contract with the state. The organization supports California’s CAASPP and ELPAC assessment programs and relied on a secure file transfer protocol (SFTP) site to share testing data with CDE.
The organization spotted unauthorized activity on the site on September 25, but the earliest access dates back to late May.
“The investigation determined that an unauthorized party used a compromised login credential at various times during the period from May 22, 2026 to September 18, 2026 to access the SFTP site to copy files containing California student information,” according to the CDE’s breach notice.
No victim count has been provided, but the notice says, “Information about California students, including but not limited to all students enrolled in the three previous school years, was accessed and copied.”
CDE’s own enrollment figures put that in perspective: more than 5.7 million students were enrolled in California public schools in 2025-2026. La couleur d’une étoile dépend presque uniquement de sa température. Une étoile froide est orangée, une étoile très chaude d’un bleu pâle. Quand une étoile de la taille du Soleil épuise son combustible, elle laisse derrière elle une naine blanche, et les astronomes pensaient que ces astres morts suivaient eux aussi la règle des couleurs. Mark Hollands, chercheur en astrophysique à l’université de Warwick, a voulu vérifier cette idée avec trois collègues. Leur équipe a converti la lumière de naines blanches réparties dans tout le ciel en couleurs perçues par l’œil humain, et l’une d’elles est ressortie d’un vert chartreuse. Il faut remonter jusqu’aux restes de son ancien système planétaire pour comprendre d’où vient ce vert.
Du sodium tombé d’anciennes planètes
Les chercheurs estiment la température de surface de WD J1330+6435 à environ 4 000 °C, d’après leur étude parue mi-octobre dans la revue RAS Techniques and Instruments. The full system comprises a Wi-Fi transmitter, a Wi-Fi receiver, and the WiFireNet AI.
When ordinary Wi-Fi signals encounter an object in their path, they penetrate and bounce off in ways specific to that object, based on its shape, orientation, and material. The challenges extend well beyond just performance. This will require new tools and methodologies, as well as some new design approaches.
“AI is leaving the screen,” says Anthony Matarazzo, head of physical AI, digital twins, simulation-driven AI, and accelerated computing at Synopsys. “It is no longer about generating text or code. articles.title: How far can we push computing?

How far can we push computing?
Nowadays big advances are made by scaling up—think more chips packed into ever-bigger data centers. But as we near the ceiling of what we can build, there’s still plenty of room below, at the fundamental physical limits of computing.
MIT Technology Review Explains: Let our writers untangle the complex, messy world of science and technology to help you understand what’s coming next. You can read more from the series here.
On the evening of December 29, 1959, at an American Physical Society meeting at Caltech, the physicist Richard Feynman gave a lecture called “There’s Plenty of Room at the Bottom,” on how we might manipulate and control things on an extremely small scale. There is no physical law stopping us from writing the entire Encyclopædia Britannica on the head of a pin, he argued, or from storing every book ever written in something the size of a dust speck—or, ultimately, from arranging matter atom by atom. Biology already did versions of this (a living cell keeps its instructions in a wisp of DNA), so all of this was plainly permitted by the laws of physics. We simply had not built the tools yet.
In other words, there was plenty of room at the bottom. He was right, and for decades we descended into that space almost for free. The transistor—the switch at the heart of computer chips—repeatedly halved in size so that chips doubled in density; a computer that once filled a room now fits inside a watch. The attackers were observed dropping a cryptocurrency miner built on XMRig. Later that day, a second program called myawesomeproxy also appeared on the honeypot. The researcher identified it as proxy software, and it shows a notice saying that anyone running it agrees to the potential use of their internet traffic.

articles.title: The gap between financial inclusion and access to credit in Nigeria
articles.summary:
This is Follow the Money, our weekly series that unpacks the earnings, business, and scaling strategies of African fintechs, financial institutions, companies, and governments. A new edition drops every Monday.
Nigeria has made progress in bringing more people into the formal financial system, but having a bank account does not necessarily mean being able to obtain a loan. While more Nigerians can now access financial services, borrowing costs, limited credit histories, and irregular incomes still shape who can obtain formal credit and on what terms.
According to the 2026 Access to Financial Services in Nigeria (A2F) survey by Enhancing Financial Innovation & Access (EFInA), formal financial inclusion rose to 73%, up from 64% in 2023. The proportion of adults excluded from the financial system fell from 26% to 21%. EFInA estimates that 87.2 million Nigerian adults are now formally included, yet only about 12 million (10%) access formal credit.
These figures show that financial inclusion is not the same as access to credit. Financial inclusion encompasses access to and use of services such as payments, savings, insurance and borrowing. A person may have a bank account, receive payments digitally and save through a formal institution without qualifying for a loan.

These are not cynical questions. They reflect the logic of venture capital, where investors put capital at risk expecting substantial returns and founders pursue growth, scale and eventually liquidity.
But there is a question we ask far less often: Are we building the companies we actually want to own, or the companies our funding models encourage us to build?
When success changes meaning

These were successful entrepreneurs by conventional measures. Yet their experiences had changed how they thought about ownership, ambition and what they ultimately wanted from building a business. articles.title: New Tools Let Users Edit and Load Modified VBIOS on GeForce RTX GPUs Without Flashing
articles.summary:
Sunday, October 18th 2026
New Tools Let Users Edit and Load Modified VBIOS on GeForce RTX GPUs Without Flashing
A developer who goes by Panchovix has released three tools that let NVIDIA GeForce RTX 50, RTX 40, and RTX 30-series owners run a modified VBIOS without writing anything to the card's flash chip. The first is a VBIOS editor for Windows and Linux that can change power limits, voltage ceilings, current (OCP) limits, fan channels, and the core and memory offset ranges. Edited images keep NVIDIA's original signature, which no longer matches, so they can't be flashed with nvflash. Patched tools did break NVIDIA's BIOS signature lock for crossflashing back in 2023, but this approach skips flashing altogether. On Windows, the loader stores the edited image in the GPU's driver registry key, where the driver picks it up as an override every time the device starts, and it only needs a quick GPU restart. The Linux loader instead patches NVIDIA's open kernel modules so the GSP firmware starts with the custom image, with Fedora 43 being the only distro tested on real hardware so far.
The screenshots show how this works in practice. On what appears to be an RTX 5090 Founders Edition ROM, the board power ceiling went from 600 W to 700 W and the NVVDD and MSVDD voltage ceilings from 1,110 mV to 1,150 mV. Orange et SFR épinglés lors d’un relevé parisien

Yet these differences do not neatly explain where fibre infrastructure has been built, raising questions about what else drives investment.
Administrative reforms and project-specific concessions may help offset high fees, but there is little evidence that they do so systematically. The Lagos State Infrastructure Maintenance and Regulatory Agency (LASIMRA) describes itself as a one-stop regulator for utility infrastructure, and the state has announced an online permitting system to streamline approvals for fibre, masts and towers. However, the announcement does not establish whether the system has reduced processing times or costs or removed requirements such as environmental approvals.
Ogun has also reportedly waived RoW charges for a specific 250-kilometre MainOne deployment, but that historical concession does not establish that similar incentives are generally available today. There is no verified evidence of a telecom-specific tax-break programme that explains the substantial fibre networks in these high-fee states. Without access to operators’ permits, concession agreements and investment decisions, it remains unclear whether incentives offset the charges or whether companies invest despite them.

Per-project audits of the moratoriums indicate that they tend to miss the site, the permit, or the timeline.

articles.title: This 'benchtop' nuclear fusion device could provide fuel for the next revolution in clean energy
articles.summary:
This startup is developing tiny 'benchtop' fusion devices in secret to build a more efficient nuclear reactor
Stellar power here on Earth
Nuclear fusion is how stars (including our own Sun) create their energy, and scientists are hopeful it could one day be used as a clean, abundant energy solution here on Earth. There are no carbon emissions, most of the fuel required is widely available, and it's safe: if the reaction goes wrong, it simply peters out and stops.
You might have spotted the big challenge, which is trying to fit an entire star's worth of energy production inside a power plant. Two main approaches are being explored, one using magnets to create the incredibly high temperatures and pressures required, and one using lasers — which is where the startup Cambridge Heavy Industries comes in.
As TechCrunch reports, the company is currently operating in 'stealth mode' from a lab attached to the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), but now seems ready to share some details about the technology it's developing. Inside the quest to combat Arctic fires and save the planet’s frozen carbon
These scientists hope that fire-spotting satellites, AI tools and ancient land practices could preserve the world’s vulnerable permafrost—and the vast carbon it stores.
In the middle of an especially warm July in 2021, a wildfire ignited in a thick forest of black spruce and peeling paper birch trees on the northern campus of the University of Alaska, Fairbanks.
The blaze, possibly sparked by lightning, burned across the dry carpet of feather mosses and lichen before climbing into the crowns. By the time fire agencies responded, flames had reached 12 feet in length and sent up a 500-foot column of smoke.
A few days shy of the five-year anniversary of the Yankovich Road Fire, I followed three members of the Alaska Fire Science Consortium into the boreal forest, walking along cross-country ski trails lined by feathery field horsetail.
In 2024, the organization, which hosts presentations to keep wildfire managers abreast of new developments in fire science, helped turn the area into an educational walking trail, with interpretive signs posted along the route. About a half-mile in, the horizon opened up as we reached a sparse stand of naked, blackened tree trunks, stripped of needles and neighbors.

articles.title: Typo-squatting attacks with major domains are still viable — corner cases with Cyrillic characters still evade the best checks
articles.summary:
Typo-squatting attacks with major domains are still viable — corner cases with Cyrillic characters still evade the best checks
Are you watching closely?
When the IETF decided to allow Unicode characters in domain names, many techies saw the move as commendable, but also fraught with danger, as hundreds of unique characters can look similar or identical across multiple alphabets. This can be used for typosquatting attacks, wherein bad actors create functioning websites with deliberately misspelled web addresses that look identical to the real URL, thus launching attacks against unsuspecting visitors who land on the site due to search results generated when the user mistypes an address. The Chromium browser has the most advanced ruleset for finding and preventing mischievous domains masquerading as legitimate ones, but even the best code has odd edge cases, as a blog post from Have I Been Squatted (HIBS) explains in great detail.
Using "аррӏө.com" as an example — which is in fact not identical to the real "apple.com" — the researchers show how specific combinations of characters can still evade multiple layers of protection, thanks to the particular circumstances surrounding the use of specific Cyrillic characters. This alphabet has lookalikes for many Latin letters. For example, а → a, е → e, о → o, р → p, and с → c. We forgive you if you can't spot the differences.

articles.title: Training AIs to Solve CAPTCHAs - Schneier on Security
articles.summary:
Training AIs to Solve CAPTCHAs
Interesting research:
Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can solve visual CAPTCHAs without task-specific training, but the agents built on them approach every challenge from scratch. For such an agent, the hundredth instance of a familiar puzzle costs as much time and compute as the first. Specialized detectors invert the trade-off, answering in milliseconds but only for categories they were trained on. Neither improves with exposure. We study what changes when a solver improves with use. Our system pairs a fine-tuned YOLOv8 detector with an open-weight VLM behind a confidence-based router, and runs entirely from screenshots and operating-system input events, with no browser automation or DOM access. It reaches 85.4% overall and 84.2% macro accuracy across 16 classes, exceeding either component alone. Every answer VLM produces also serves as a training label, so the detector absorbs categories it was never trained for, typically after one or two encounters and without human annotation. The same loop also repairs it. A CAPTCHA operator can perturb images against the publicly released detector and drive its accuracy to 0%, but the perturbations leave VLM untouched, and its labels let the detector recover. Under a year-long simulated arms race in which the CAPTCHA operator re-crafts its perturbations each month, the solver recovers every round, and a cheap ~70%-accurate open-weight teacher hardens it as effectively as a perfect oracle. PlayStation 6 Could Get Sony's Own Frame Generation Technology, Patent Suggests
Sony has a new patent application that describes its own take on frame generation, and the PlayStation 6 seems like the obvious target, though no console is named. Titled "Generation Super Sampling," the filing (US 2026/0320740 A1) was published on October 15 and lists Sony engineer Denis Dupeyron as the inventor. It describes an encoder neural network that turns a newly rendered frame into a compact embedding, and a decoder network that uses it to predict the next frame. Optional inputs include motion vectors and recent controller inputs, which help the model guess where the player is heading. That frame is displayed while the next real one is still rendering.
The filing points out that existing methods insert a generated frame between two real ones, which means waiting for both and adding delay. Sony's version predicts forward from a single frame, with the goal of smoothing out hitching in heavy scenes without lowering visual quality. It can also predict several frames at once, and there's a simpler non-AI fallback that shifts blocks of pixels along their motion vectors. Apparently, the model trains on the video stream itself, comparing each guess with the real next frame, so no human labeling is needed. Based on Gemma 4 and released under the Apache 2.0 license, Google's EmbeddingGemma 2 is a compact, open-weight, multimodal embedding model designed to make semantic search and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) more efficient while optimizing performance for on-device deployment.
Designed to run on consumer hardware such as mobile devices and laptops, EmbeddingGemma 2 delivers low-latency semantic representations for on-device applications, like search, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), classification, and clustering.
Thanks to its multimodal capabilities, EmbeddingGemma 2 supports a wide range of retrieval tasks, including finding relevant documents, screenshots, and recordings in response to a query, searching source code using natural language, and retrieving video content based on textual descriptions.
EmbeddingGemma 2's key feature, Google says, is its ability to represent text, code, images, video, and audio in a unified 768-dimensional embedding space. This enables developers to build retrieval systems that search across different media types without maintaining separate, incompatible embedding spaces for different media types.
Despite coming from different modalities, the embeddings generated by EmbeddingGemma 2 occupy the same dimensional space and can be compared on their semantic similarity.

articles.title: MIT engineers build soft 3D shape-sensing skin for gaming and VR — tracks 3D movement and touch with sub-half-centimeter error
articles.summary:
MIT engineers build soft 3D shape-sensing skin for gaming and VR — tracks 3D movement and touch with sub-half-centimeter error
Although it still works with a few fibers cut, a garment would need many more, much thinner ones.
MIT engineers have built a soft, wearable shape-sensing sheet with self-tracking movement that could be useful for controlling games, virtual reality, and physical therapy applications, reports MIT News. The technology, which leverages optical fibers to track the sheet’s own 3D shape, keeps its error below half a centimeter in lab tests. Qifan Yu, an MIT mechanical engineering graduate student on the team, put rigid-sensor designs at around 1 to 2 cm and called the result “at least on par with existing technologies.” The sheet also still works even when damaged, but the fibers remain thicker than ideal for garments.
The news follows a paper, “Toward fully soft and multifunctional shape sensing via optical waveguide arrays,” recently published in Advanced Intelligent Systems. It details that the waveguides respond to bending in both directions, “bi-directional,” with the array laid out to discern shapes. Combined fiber responses mean fewer sensing elements are needed, and that can also improve damage resilience. The fibers respond to pressure, so they can sense external force, such as a press on the forearm in a physical therapy demo.

Sahi’s Dale Vaz wants an AI financial team in every pocket
From plain-language trading strategies to a Discipline Score that flags overtrading, Sahi’s Kyro shows how AI could give every Indian investor a personal team of financial agents, in their own language.
Opening a trading account in India now takes minutes. Knowing what to do once you’re in is much harder.
This gap was the focus of Dale Vaz’s keynote at TechSparks 2026. The co-founder and CEO of fintech company Sahi argued that the last decade of fintech solved the issue of access, but not outcomes.
“Everybody here has a broking app,” Vaz told the audience. “But when you think about outcomes, do people really feel confident about what to do with their money? The numbers indicate most of us are still struggling.”
The intent-capability gap
Vaz described a familiar pattern among retail investors. People start investing, then struggle to make sense of their portfolios. A bad day in the market leaves them unsure about whether to buy, sell, or quit altogether.
The cause, he said, is complexity: too much jargon, too much data, and too many tools. Investors are left with two poor choices. They can spend years becoming experts, or they can trust someone promising guaranteed returns.
Regulator-led investor education has helped, Vaz said, but a wide gap remains between people’s intent to grow their money and their capability to do it.

articles.title: Jubilee, FSD Africa partner with 7 BimaLab insurtechs to pilot inclusive insurance in Kenya - Disrupt Africa
articles.summary:
East African financial services group Jubilee and development agency FSD Africa have partnered with seven insurtech startups from the BimaLab Africa accelerator network to develop and pilot affordable insurance products for underserved Kenyans.
BimaLab, an FSD Africa initiative, has supported 135 startups across 28 African countries over the past six years, helping develop more than 300 insurance solutions that now reach over 6.5 million customers.
The programme targets SMEs, informal sector workers, farmers and low-income households, segments that remain largely uninsured. East Africa is estimated to have more than 10 million SMEs, which account for over 70 per cent of jobs, yet insurance penetration among the segment averages about one per cent.
The seven firms – Dukatech Solutions, Aura Insure Technologies, Inclusivity Solutions, DPE, Fiinovate, Agrails and Ibisa Network – were selected through a competitive process from BimaLab’s alumni network. They will go through an eight-week product co-creation process with Jubilee before joint pilots kick off in Kenya next month.
The work will focus on three areas – low-cost bundled and embedded insurance distribution, insurance solutions for SME ecosystems, and wellness and engagement models that link customers to health and care services. Successful solutions could later be rolled out in other East African markets.

articles.title: The Future of Web Apps: Will AI Agents Generate UIs on the Fly?
articles.summary:
Rachel Lee Nabors, former React core team member, dives into the architecture and philosophy behind local-first applications, exploring how small language models (SLMs) running directly on-device can deliver privacy-focused, low-latency, and cost-effective alternatives to cloud-hosted LLM wrappers. Rachel shares key insights on evaluating models with golden datasets and leveraging client-side AI for moderation and social content aggregation.
The discussion also looks ahead to the future of web and application architectures in an AI-driven ecosystem. From the potential rise of OS-level personal agents and dynamic UI rendering standards like A2UI, to the evolving skill set required of software engineers.
Key Takeaways
- Building apps local-first delivers fast, offline capability for users while keeping cloud infrastructure costs low for developers.
- Utilizing SLMs locally (like Llama 3.2B) avoids high API costs, reduces latency, and protects PII compared to large cloud LLMs.
- Systematic evaluation using golden datasets is essential for right-sizing models and picking the best option for specific tasks like summarization or moderation.
- OS-level personal agents and standardized UI schemas (like A2UI) may replace traditional web apps and native interfaces for consumption.
- Software engineering is moving beyond basic code generation towards computer science fundamentals, system design, and AI collaboration.
