EmulateHeap als Relikt von Windows 95
Bei dem Relikt handelt es sich laut Windows Latest um EmulateHeap. Dieser Kompatibilitäts-Patch ermöglicht es den Nutzer:innen von modernen Microsoft-Betriebssystemen, alte Software oder Spiele aus der Ära von Windows 95 zum Laufen zu bringen.
EmulateHeap kopiert die Eigenschaften des Speichermanagers von Windows 95 für neuere Systeme. Denn der hält gerade für Games Vorteile bereit, die spätere Inkarnationen von Windows nicht haben.
Microsoft änderte für SimCity Code von Windows 95
Wenn Windows Programme ausführt, greifen die temporär auf Speicherkapazitäten zurück. Sobald man die Applikation beendet, wird der Speicherplatz wieder freigegeben.
Doch manchmal kann es zu einem Bug namens Use-after-free kommen. Dabei greift ein Programm auf einen Speicherbereich zu, nachdem der bereits freigegeben wurde. Dies kann zu einem Absturz führen.

articles.title: Anthropic says it’s committing 5% of its shares to a ‘public benefit fund’ | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Anthropic announced today that it’s creating a “public benefit fund” that will give the company “increased flexibility and scale” to support projects for societal good.
Anthropic said that it will commit 5% of its shares to the fund — structured as a wholly-owned entity within the company — with the option to contribute an additional 2% for every 50% increase in Anthropic’s value. And it offered some broad-strokes ideas for how this money might actually be used, such as “large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations.”
There’s also the impact that AI might have on the job market, which Anthropic has already committed $200 million to study. But the company said, “Given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed. The Fund will have the versatility to pursue them.”
Anthropic’s announcement comes as the AI industry faces increasingly negative public sentiment, which CEO Dario Amodei has described as “fundamentally a crisis of trust.”
If you’re wondering who will actually decide which public benefits are worth funding, Anthropic said it will share more information about structure and governance in the coming months.

articles.title: Intel Core i5-4670K Gets a New Cinebench R11.5 Record, 13 Years After Launch
articles.summary:
Sunday, October 18th 2026
Intel Core i5-4670K Gets a New Cinebench R11.5 Record, 13 Years After Launch
Overclocker Luumi has taken the top spot in HWBot's Cinebench R11.5 rankings for the Intel Core i5-4670K, beating a record that had stood for around 12 years. Running the 2013 Haswell quad-core at 6,301 MHz under liquid nitrogen, Luumi scored 10.8 cb, just edging out Strat's previous 10.76 cb at 6,249 MHz. That's roughly 66% above the chip's 3.8 GHz boost clock, which is quite a lot for a four-core, four-thread part built on Intel's 22 nm process. The top of the leaderboard is tight as well, with Moose83 sitting third at 10.74 cb out of 187 submissions. Of course, this is a record for the i5-4670K category, not an overall Cinebench R11.5 world record. Luumi also has a history with Cinebench, having set an 8-core world record on an EVGA Z390 Dark back in 2018.
The test bench was period-correct too. Luumi used an ASRock Z97 OC Formula, the same board that pushed a Core i7-4790K past 7 GHz back in 2014, along with 4 GB of XPG DDR3 running at 2,708 MT/s with 8-12-7-28 timings and a Corsair AXi 1600 power supply. The run was done on Windows 7, as HWBot's R11.5 rules apparently don't allow pre-Skylake Intel chips on newer versions of Windows without BenchMate. Haswell is no stranger to extreme clocks, as the Core i7-4770K was overclocked to 7 GHz before it even launched in 2013. articles.title: Official DLSS 5 running on unsupported games delivers up to 90% better performance than the leaked version — Nvidia says the new NR model uses 20% less VRAM and processes neural workloads up to 2x faster
articles.summary:
Official DLSS 5 running on unsupported games delivers up to 90% better performance than the leaked version — Nvidia says the new NR model uses 20% less VRAM and processes neural workloads up to 2x faster
Nvidia's new Neural Rendering model is smaller but better.
A new version of DLSS 5 on NBA 2K27 was just released, and modders have already extracted it and are running it on unsupported games. Modders are comparing performance between the older and newer Neural Rendering (NR) model and found it up to 40% faster than the previous one.
While many are still experimenting with leaked and first-release builds, Renan Maniero has already extracted the new 310.9.16.0 DLSS NR build, letting other modders use it in unsupported games and compare performance. Gaming Optimized on X compared the new NR model to the old one and found massive improvements of up to 90% in The Witcher 3 running DLSS 5 natively.
Running a full NR model to modify your game's image is resource-intensive, just as LLMs require a lot of RAM; DLSS NR does, too. To improve performance, Nvidia made the AI model 24% smaller, using 20% less VRAM at 4K, and, according to Nvidia, processes its neural rendering workload up to 2x faster.

- Effective agentic architectures require bounded autonomy, evaluation loops, and hybrid deterministic fallback systems.

articles.title: JEP 543 Finalizes Structured Concurrency in JDK 28, Ending Seven Preview Rounds
articles.summary:
JEP 543, Structured Concurrency, has been integrated into JDK 28, bringing the StructuredTaskScope API in java.util.concurrent to final status with no API changes from JDK 27's seventh preview. For codebases already on JDK 27, the migration comes down to recompiling without --enable-preview.
Finalization concludes the longest preview cycle of any Project Loom feature. Structured concurrency debuted as an incubator API in JEP 428 (JDK 19) and JEP 437 (JDK 20), then progressed through seven previews: JEP 453 (JDK 21), JEP 462 (JDK 22), JEP 480 (JDK 23), JEP 499 (JDK 24), JEP 505 (JDK 25), JEP 525 (JDK 26), and JEP 533 (JDK 27). Across every iteration, the core objective has been to treat groups of related subtasks running in different threads as a single unit of work, ensuring that a failure in one subtask cancels the others and that the parent scope cannot exit before all child threads have terminated. Traditional ExecutorService and Future pipelines do not enforce those boundaries: a parent method can return while subtasks continue running in the background, and a subtask failure surfaces only when a caller eventually invokes Future.get().
The API centers on StructuredTaskScope<T, R, R_X extends Throwable>, a sealed interface opened through static factory methods rather than public constructors. The zero-argument open() factory returns a scope whose join() method waits for all subtasks to succeed, cancels the rest on the first failure, and throws ExecutionException:

articles.title: Se sigue buscando al autor de la presa que convirtió un río de los Pirineos en su piscina privada durante dos años
articles.summary:
En cualquier pueblo de montaña, el río es la piscina del verano. Ya lo contábamos a propósito de las piscinas naturales andaluzas. Pero mientras Madrid quiere construirse la piscina más grande de España, lo que no es habitual ver es a alguien derivando parte de un río para montarse su propia obra. Y eso es lo que hizo alguien en Osséja, un municipio de los Pirineos franceses: levantó una barrera en el cauce del Vanéra para que el agua se remansara y tener una poza donde bañarse. Ha estado así dos años. Hasta el pasado viernes 9 de octubre, que entró una excavadora Kubota y retiró las piedras, según cuenta Diario Vasco.
Dónde. No ha sido en territorio español. Osséja está en la Cerdaña francesa, dentro del departamento de los Pirineos Orientales. El Vanéra, que en catalán se llama Llavanera, es un río transfronterizo con España, según L’Indépendant. Tras un tiempo recopilando información, los equipos técnicos del ayuntamiento entraron con la máquina en el lecho del río para desmontar una presa levantada sin permiso. Los pescadores ya habían dado la voz de alarma. Según L’Indépendant, la asociación detectó la obra hacía meses y avisó de que se veían cada vez menos peces en el río.
En la operación participó también la asociación La Fario de la Vanéra, y contó con el visto bueno de la Dirección Departamental de los Territorios y del Mar (DDTM) y de la Oficina Francesa de la Biodiversidad (OFB). Un equipo del Laboratorio de Ciencias de la Computación e Inteligencia Artificial del MIT (CSAIL) dejó a un agente de inteligencia artificial sin ninguna tarea asignada en una isla virtual durante treinta horas, y el programa respondió construyendo templos, memoriales e inventando sus propios juegos.

articles.title: Pinterest Uses Event Time Watermarks to Finalize Petabyte Scale Data Partitions
articles.summary:
Pinterest has introduced an event time-based partition finalization mechanism for its next-generation database ingestion framework, allowing downstream jobs to determine when streaming data is sufficiently complete to consume. The approach uses Apache Flink to measure event time progress and Apache Iceberg metadata to publish a non-regressing finalization watermark, addressing a challenge in continuous Change Data Capture (CDC) ingestion where data can arrive after a partition’s wall clock interval has ended.
Pinterest’s ingestion framework uses CDC, Kafka, Flink, Spark and Iceberg to move database changes from MySQL, TiDB and KVStore into analytical tables. Pinterest says the platform supports petabyte-scale data and thousands of pipelines, with online changes typically available within 15 minutes to an hour. Unlike the previous batch-based approach, where job completion indicated that a partition was ready, streaming ingestion continuously commits changes without an equivalent completion point.

On est victime de la défaillance de cette entreprise qui nous a fait de belles promesses. On s’est fait avoir ! ».
En septembre dernier, lors d’un conseil communautaire, la collectivité à donc voté la mise à la casse de ces trois bus à hydrogène. Une entreprise spécialisée va maintenant se charger de désosser les véhicules et de recycler leurs différents composants. When people talk about technology infrastructure, they usually mean semiconductors, data centres, and AI models. But the layer that decides how well these technologies work is the data underneath them, and India still has to build it.
At a panel discussion on 'The invisible infrastructure of the new tech order' at TechSparks 2026, moderated by Chhavi Mahajan, Chief Content Officer, YourStory, the panellists said India’s advantage will come from owning trusted, context-rich data in fields ranging from language AI to biotech.
Arvind Pani, Founder, CoreMantle, an AI data intelligence startup, said data is the one part of the technology stack that cannot be swapped out. “You can continue to replace compute. You can continue to replace the application, but you cannot replace the data,” he said.
Ankit Bagaria, Co-founder and CEO, Loopworm, an insect biotechnology company, said the gap is especially wide in biopharma, where too much work still happens through trial and error. Better data, he said, could cut the time it takes to bring a product to market.

Aquí hay gente que no lo lava hasta que lo quita allá por el mes de marzo, pero en el campo de la alergología las recomendaciones apuntan a que hay que ser un poco más constantes, sobre todo si somos personas sensibles a los ácaros.
Hay mitos que dicen que un edredón nórdico sin lavar durante seis meses acumula hasta 20.000 ácaros vivos, lo que puede hacer saltar todas las alarmas. Pero la realidad es que no es algo que esté del todo contrastado y el estudio en el que se basa cuenta con mucho sesgo a sus espaldas.
Y es que ahora mismo no tenemos un estudio científico que nos diga una frecuencia de lavado estrella, pero sí que hay recomendaciones que apuntan a que la funda nórdica habría que lavarla cada dos semanas a 60 ºC, ya que la grasa corporal y los ácaros terminan traspasando la tela hacia el interior del relleno.
El relleno no necesita un lavado constante, como apunta un ensayo hecho sobre niños asmáticos que nos apunta a que hay que lavar el edredón y la almohada cada tres meses. Sin embargo, los fabricantes de los plumones relajan esta frecuencia y sugieren hacerlo tan solo una vez al año.

Trouver un angle, développer une idée, construire une argumentation, prendre une décision ou comprendre un sujet compliqué… Il n’est plus rare aujourd’hui de faire appel à l’intelligence artificielle dès les premières étapes de notre raisonnement. On retient certaines de ses propositions, on les retravaille (ou pas), le plus souvent sans se demander ce qu’on aurait imaginé sans elles.
Mais que se passe-t-il lorsque des centaines de millions de personnes s’appuient sur les mêmes outils pour alimenter leur réflexion ? À force de faire de l’IA une source habituelle d’inspiration, nos idées pourraient finir par se ressembler. Un risque d’homogénéisation cognitive qui concerne la diversité de nos productions, certes, mais soulève aussi la question de l’influence des modèles sur nos jugements et, à plus long terme, sur notre manière de penser.

Apple tightened its developer guidelines over the weekend to ban apps that use AI to create offensive content, as well as those that masquerade as regular apps to pass the App Store review process and then turn into nudify apps, or surface those features prominently.
The company updated its guidelines with strong language around AI and user-generated content, and how app developers should include enough preventative measures to moderate objectionable or offensive content.
“Apps that host user-generated content are required to filter objectionable material, give users a way to report offensive content, and let users block abusive accounts. Apps containing hidden or undocumented features are also prohibited on the App Store, including apps that misrepresent their purpose during review and only reveal harmful capabilities — such as “nudification” — after approval, a tactic commonly known as bait-and-switch,” the company said in a blog post.
Apple said that it will remove apps that add features not present in the version submitted for App Store review.
The iPhone maker has also updated the language in its legal section to reinforce that it will bar apps promoting human trafficking and exploitation of children.
Apple said last year its review process blocked over 150,000 apps from reaching users, and removed 193,000 developer accounts on account of fraud and abuse.

Virtual reality is in a bit of a weird place right now. After a lot of unfulfilled promise in the 1990s, it came back strong with the 2016 release of the Oculus Rift. For a while, it looked like VR, AR, XR, the metaverse, or whatever you wanted to call it, was going to be huge. Mark Zuckerberg was certainly convinced, and even Apple got in on the hype with its Vision Pro.
But by then momentum for alternate realities of every acronym was already in steady decline, and it only dwindled from there. The rate of development of new headsets has slowed, with many companies (including Apple) scaling back or shelving their efforts. While new releases like the Steam Frame and Pimax Dream Air are still happening, many of the most interesting developments in the space these days are on the enthusiast front.
That’s right, DIY VR is a thing, and with a couple hundred dollars in components, plus many hours of your time, you too can enter the immersive world of virtual reality while also experiencing the highs and lows of soldering, firmware flashing, and 3D printing. I rode that rollercoaster myself and learned why this is still a decidedly niche movement.

articles.summary:
The science of deep sleep and how Duroflex Airboost helps you get more of it
India’s newest sleep technology is designed to enhance the N3 stage, the body’s repair shift, for better recovery, immunity, and stress resilience.
You can get enough sleep and still not get enough recovery.
We obsess over sleep duration, the “eight hours” metric, but duration alone doesn't tell the whole story. What matters just as much is depth. Deep sleep is the stage where the body does its heaviest lifting: repairing tissue, consolidating memory, and resetting the hormones that govern everything from appetite to stress. Yet for a growing number of people, deep sleep is the first thing to go missing, even when total sleep time looks normal on paper.
The different stages of sleep
Sleep isn't a single, uniform state. It cycles through distinct stages roughly every 90 minutes, each with a different job.
Light sleep (N1 and N2) acts as the transition zone; the body slows down, heart rate drops, and brain activity shifts into slower rhythms. This stage makes up the bulk of a typical night, but it's largely preparatory.
Deep sleep, or N3 stage (also called slow-wave sleep), is where the real restorative work happens. Brain waves slow dramatically, blood pressure and breathing reach their lowest points, and the body redirects energy toward physical repair, regenerating muscle, strengthening the immune system, and clearing metabolic waste from the brain.

One more step into the future of air combat.
The U.S. Air Force has just successfully conducted an airborne test where an F-22 Raptor pilot directed an Anduril YFQ-44A Fury drone during simulated combat. The successful test is part of the USAF’s Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA), which seeks to integrate drones into fighter squadrons. These uncrewed aircraft must be able to respond to the fighter pilot’s tactical commands and then operate autonomously, though. That’s because fighter pilots already have a heavy workload — flying their own aircraft, managing sensor data, threat assessment, and weapons release decisions — so requiring them to manually fly a drone is next to impossible. Command integration means that the F-22 Raptor pilot could assign the Fury drone a specific tactical task, like monitoring for and engaging enemy air defenses, while they focus on the primary mission, such as taking out enemy fighters.

Agility Robotics setzt deshalb auf besonders leichte Akkus mit hoher Leistungsdichte, die also viel Energie pro Kilogramm abgeben können.
Mit der neuen Technik könne Digit 5 täglich mehr als zwei komplette Arbeitsschichten absolvieren, teilt Agility Robotics mit. Orange pour les plus froides, blanches comme le Soleil, bleu pâle pour les plus chaudes : la couleur d'une étoile se lit d'ordinaire comme un thermomètre. Les naines blanches, ces résidus ultradenses que laissent les étoiles de type solaire en fin de vie, passaient pour suivre la même règle. The position change, which was likely not an accident as fuel is scarce, is probably a provocation and an attempt to spy on the satellite.
LeoLabs said in a statement Friday that the movement “appears to be a deliberate approach” toward ICEYE-X36, with uncertain intent and behavior that “warrants continued monitoring.” Roughly 3 miles is too close for comfort in satellite terms: there is no strict legal limit on how close satellites can get, but countries generally keep at least 6 miles (9.7 km) apart, University of Mississippi space law professor Aaron Brynildson told Axios. The approach was made without the owner’s consent, and Russia hasn’t said what the military satellite carries.

El papel de cocina presenta un problema similar. Aunque a simple vista resulte suave, su superficie tiene una dureza mayor a la que parece, lo que lo vuelve perjudicial para el cristal. Joshua Bird shared a video of how they created it on YouTube, highlighting the unique technique they used to maintain controllability and stability. The design used a combination of a hinged propeller, rapid changes to the motor’s rotation speed, and a custom flight controller and motor controller firmware that allowed the motor to react to necessary changes in under 0.2 milliseconds.
Most rotary wing aircraft require a mechanism to counteract the torque generated by the motor or engine and to change its flight direction, typically with the use of a swash plate to change rotor disk attitude and a secondary propeller. While this method has been effective for decades, it has made rotary-wing aircraft heavier and more complex. This single-motor drone cut the need for a secondary mechanism by constantly adjusting the speed of the motor — speeding it up produces more reaction torque while slowing it down applies opposite reaction torque. La vidéosurveillance algorithmique (VSA), qui sont pourrait-on dire des caméras « augmentées » à l'intelligence artificielle, a-t-elle scruté les manifestations contre la vie chère qui ont secoué plusieurs villes de France samedi ? Rien ne permet de l'affirmer, et pour cause : le droit la réserve aux concerts, aux matchs et, depuis cet été, à certains bâtiments jugés sensibles. Avec plus de 2 000 interpellations au compteur et un ministre de l'Intérieur décidé à remonter la piste des pilleurs image par image, la surveillance des cortèges est, c'est une certitude, loin d'être une affaire classée, des drones préfectoraux à la reconnaissance faciale.

Née dans les cartons des Jeux olympiques de Paris, la VSA tient moins du physionomiste que du vigile, du moins sur le papier. Cuando empecé a jugar a las consolas solo podías ser de dos bandos: o de Mario o de Sonic. O lo que es lo mismo: tenías que decidirte entre Nintendo y su Super Nintendo o Sega y su Mega Drive. Las dos empresas marcaban el rumbo de los videojuegos a comienzos de los 90, al menos en el ámbito doméstico. Y cada una necesitaba distinguirse con algún rasgo único. En Sega optaron por la velocidad.
Sonic iba rápido, la Mega Drive no. El hardware de la máquina no estaba mal para la época, pero tenía ciertas limitaciones. El obstáculo estaba, principalmente, en el procesador: el Motorola 68000 que montaba, a 7,67 MHz, era un chip bastante apto, pero carecía de un componente especializado en cálculos matemáticos complejos. Sus 64 KB de memoria RAM tampoco ayudaban (con otros 64 KB dedicados a vídeo).
Dado que Mega Drive necesitaba un Sonic a la altura para vender la máquina, en Sega le encargaron el proyecto a Yuji Naka, cocreador de la saga. Según explicaba en este vídeo con motivo del vigésimo aniversario de Sonic, Yuji tenía claro que los programadores no podían renunciar a la velocidad.
Naka lo explicaba así al recordar el origen del proyecto:
"Me gustan las cosas rápidas y pensé que sería interesante crear un juego en el que, cuanto más hábil te volvieras, menos tiempo necesitaras para completar un nivel".

Después de un descanso, parte del grupo volvió a ver las mismas imágenes. El resto vio versiones alteradas por inteligencia artificial, con expresiones faciales modificadas, personal militar insertado o señales de cambio climático añadidas digitalmente.
La prueba de memoria posterior arrojó un resultado que sorprendió a la propia investigadora. Quienes habían visto las fotografías manipuladas mostraron un aumento marcado de falsos recuerdos, y además confiaban más en esos recuerdos inexistentes que el resto de los participantes.
“Considero que todo esto es muy peligroso, básicamente”, dijo Maes, según consignó The Washington Post.

articles.title: Why AI coding is widening the software security gap

Why AI coding is widening the software security gap
The impact of AI code on security
AI coding assistants are no longer experimental. In organizations that have adopted them, AI is responsible for roughly half of committed code. The question is, therefore, no longer whether developers will use AI, but whether security programs can govern what those systems produce. AI-generated code is remarkably good at producing syntactically correct code, with a 99.9% pass rate. In contrast, security performance tells a very different story.
As it stands, the average security pass rate is only 56%, meaning roughly 44% of tested code-generation tasks introduce a known vulnerability. As the volume of AI-generated code increases while security performance remains largely unchanged, organizations risk introducing more vulnerable code into their development environments. As a result, software vulnerabilities are now the top breach entry point at 31%, overtaking stolen credentials.
Chris Wysopal is Chief Security Evangelist at Veracode.
Closing that gap means rethinking how security fits into AI-assisted development. Organizations need to make security part of the development process from the start, choose models with risk in mind and verify code in context before it reaches production. The goal is not to slow developers down; it’s to make sure security can operate at the same speed and scale as the software being created.

articles.title: You would not use a Ferrari for the school run. Why are you doing it for AI?

You would not use a Ferrari for the school run. Why are you doing it for AI?
Matching AI workloads to the right models and infrastructure
Not everyone owns a Ferrari, but I’m sure those who do rarely use it to pick their children up from school. It is less energy-efficient, not as safe or spacious and may garner unwanted attention. The analogy is simple: in AI, you do not always need the most powerful tool for everyday tasks.
It is a trap many businesses have fallen into since the first wave of AI, when early adopters were trying to prove they could access the cutting edge of the technology. Everyone wanted to have the most powerful AI model, the most sought-after accelerators and the fastest route from the pilot stage to implementation.

articles.title: Change is constant across your IT estate. But is it under control?
articles.summary:
Change is constant across your IT estate. But is it under control?
The risks of unmanaged change in IT estates
There’s never been so much change happening across an IT estate. And it’s constant. On a day-to-day basis, IT teams might be creating and monitoring user permissions, deploying any scheduled operating system (OS) updates or integrating new third-party software tools. This is not to mention all the change carried out by external providers, outsourced teams and employees.
Change itself is not a problem. Indeed, it’s essential for ongoing security, resilience and modernization. Change that isn’t actively managed, however, is a different story. This could be change that goes unnoticed, like an external patch that automatically updates a system without IT oversight, or change that is forced, like rushing an OS upgrade to meet an impending end-of-life deadline.
Director at Cloudhouse.
The trouble is many organizations have to monitor incredibly large and complex IT estates that can contain hundreds or thousands of business-critical endpoints. And so much change is now automated or carried out by external parties. Consequently, without the right software and processes, this means that IT teams can have limited visibility into many changes taking place.
These changes might seem small or innocuous on their own. But left unmanaged, they mean systems are drifting away from their intended baseline, which adds risk to each subsequent change – and that’s when systems can fail and …

articles.title: OpenCode Console Breach May Have Exposed OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google API Keys
articles.summary:
An intruder reached a legacy system at OpenCode on the night of October 16 and may have exposed the third-party AI provider keys that users had saved in OpenCode Console, the company said.
Console is OpenCode's optional hosted service: a workspace saves its own OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google key there, and Console uses that key to call the provider so team members can use the models without ever seeing the key.
The affected group is 1.4% of Console users, all of whom have an outside provider linked, and OpenCode has told them via email to revoke those keys with each provider and replace them.
The email went out on the morning of October 17 under the subject line "Action Required: Potential provider key breach." Anyone who did not get one was not affected, OpenCode said in a post on X later that day.
The keys at risk are the ones pasted into Console. The OpenCode command-line and desktop apps keep provider keys added on the machine in a SQLite database there. The breach involves "the OpenCode Console, not OpenCode itself," co-founder Dax Raad wrote in a reply on X, and those keys "never come to us."
A provider key is a bearer credential: whoever holds a copy can run billable requests against the owner's account until the provider revokes it. Deleting the key from Console does not revoke it, and a Console budget cannot cap that use either, because Console only sees requests that pass through its own gateway.

articles.title: Unpatched Broadcom Wi-Fi Flaw Lets Attackers in Range Run Code as Root on Routers
articles.summary:
A flaw in Broadcom's Wi-Fi setup software lets an attacker within radio range run code as root on Broadcom-based routers, without the network password or any pairing step, security researcher Quentin Kaiser disclosed on October 16.
He showed the attack working against home gateways supplied by three Belgian internet providers, in one case reading the Wi-Fi password off the device and in another opening a remote shell over the air. No CVE has been assigned to the flaw, and no fix has been deployed to the affected routers, Kaiser says.
The flaw is in Broadcom's version of Wi-Fi Protected Setup (WPS), the feature that lets a device join a Wi-Fi network without the password being typed in. Broadcom's code mishandles the reassembly of fragmented WPS setup messages, so an attacker in range can send crafted messages that corrupt the router's memory. From there, Kaiser built two things: a way to read memory back off the device, and a way to run his own code on it.
Against an Orange Belgium gateway, the Askey TCG3000 read the Wi-Fi password (the PSK) from the router's stored settings, sent it back over the air, and then joined the network with it.
Against a Proximus gateway, the Sagemcom-built BBOX3V+, the exploit opened a reverse shell, a remote command line, carried over Wi-Fi frames, so no outside server was needed.

Sin embargo, en el documental You Can See Everything, dirigido por Nathan Fielder y Lance Oppenheim, Evans acepta esa comparación frente a cámara mientras discute con Holmes ideas de producto para la compañía, según reconstruyó Wired. “Podría pensar que esto fue lo más estúpido que hice”, dijo el heredero hotelero sobre su participación en el filme, en declaraciones al podcast All-In conducido por David Friedberg.

articles.title: From Email-to-Case to the Boardroom: How Inherited Agents Break Governance Built for Software
articles.summary:
In Salesforce Agentforce, the recommended way to make an agent respond to events is a Flow: a record is created or a case is updated, and the Flow passes data into the agent's prompt. Separately, Email-to-Case and Web-to-Case turn inbound customer messages into case records; it is how airlines and hotels run support intake. Both are standard, documented, as-designed features. Chained together, they produce this path:
public internet → email → case record → agent prompt → agent action → case comment → outbound reply
An unauthenticated outsider now has a route into an internal agent's instructions, and the agent's reply leaves through the same door. Nothing was misconfigured. The finding, documented by researchers in August 2026, is a clean example of how agents that arrive inside existing platforms fail: through the application around them, not the model inside them.
The risk is in the application, and the application is the thing nobody re-reviewed
Which intake features are enabled, which triggers fire, which objects are exposed to guest users, which automation passes untrusted data where, and which model version the agent is quietly calling underneath: these are the variables that decide whether the Agentforce chain is a support-queue nuisance or a data exposure. A vendor risk review performed once at procurement sees none of them, because the agent did not exist at procurement. Microsoft has announced it will pull out of a project the UK government had previously dubbed the country’s largest AI data center.
A backlog of power capacity for UK data centers means the site would not be operational until the early 2030s, prompting Microsoft’s withdrawal from the project.
The development, announced in 2025 and headed by British company Nscale, was set to be built at a site in Loughton, Essex - but the project has been mired in controversy after it was revealed in March 2026 that the site was still operating as a scaffolding yard.
Nscale data center in limbo
The data center was originally planned to be hooked up to the grid by 2027, but the UK currently does not have enough energy capacity for the more than 300 data centers still looking to connect to the energy grid. Capacity is stretched so thin that the total electricity demand for data centers is currently 60% greater than current capacity.

articles.title: Beaucoup pestent contre Parcoursup dans la rue, mais la plateforme ne sera pas supprimée, juste améliorée

Dans un contexte ô combien tendu, le gouvernement a dévoilé ce lundi 19 octobre le bilan de Parcoursup 2026, la plateforme nationale d'admission dans le supérieur que de nombreux lycéens et étudiants voudraient voir disparaître, pancartes à la main, depuis plusieurs semaines. Sur le papier, la machine fonctionne et attire, avec plus d'un million de candidats, du jamais-vu, et une écrasante majorité de lycéens repartis avec une proposition d'admission. Sauf qu'entre ce que mesurent les ministères et ce que vivent les candidats, l'écart demeure, et le communiqué officiel finit lui-même par l'admettre à demi-mot, avec la promesse de modifications, sans parler de suppression.
Parcoursup 2026, un bulletin de notes plutôt flatteur
Commençons par les chiffres, le terrain où l'exécutif se sent le plus à l'aise. La session 2026 de Parcoursup, close le 10 septembre, a réuni 1 046 000 candidats, pour un total de 25 000 formations proposées, apprentissage compris. Cela fait 66 000 de plus qu'en 2025, dont 10 000 lycéens et 23 000 étudiants en quête de réorientation. En trois ans, la foule des postulants a grossi de 129 000 personnes.

AI continues to push the boundaries in almost every task it gets given, and two new reports highlight the tech's growing capabilities when it comes to code-breaking and testing widely used encryption security protocols.
First up, Japan Today reveals that AI engineer Carter Church has used OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra model to crack a written code used by one of Napoleon Bonaparte's generals more than 200 years ago. The message dates from 1809, and mentions the positions of troops belonging to France and its allies.
The letter was sitting ignored in an online archive when Church decided to give it a go. Manually decoding the symbols, numbers, and letters could have taken weeks, but the AI was done in just six hours.
"What AI mostly brings is persistence," Church told AFP, adding that he felt "an unbelievable sense of satisfaction and excitement" when the result appeared. It was verified by patent engineer Satoshi Tomokiyo, who maintains an online list of unsolved ciphers for amateur cryptographers to tackle.

articles.title: Alerte maximale dans le cloud : une faille critique de Linux menace l’étanchéité des serveurs
articles.summary:
Une vulnérabilité découverte dans le noyau Linux menace l’isolation des machines virtuelles sur les serveurs KVM. Baptisée PwnEscape et notée 9,3/10 en gravité, elle pousse déjà plusieurs hébergeurs à prendre des mesures d’urgence.
Pour un hébergeur cloud, l’une des pires situations serait de voir un client prendre le contrôle du serveur qui héberge ses machines virtuelles. C’est précisément le risque soulevé par PwnEscape (CVE-2026-99999), une faille critique du noyau Linux révélée par les chercheurs de pwn.ai.
Le problème concerne les infrastructures utilisant KVM, une technologie de virtualisation largement répandue sous Linux. Dans les configurations exposées, un attaquant disposant de privilèges élevés dans une machine virtuelle peut exploiter son interface réseau virtuelle de type virtio pour franchir les protections qui l’isolent du serveur hôte. Il pourrait alors compromettre ce serveur et, potentiellement, les ressources d’autres clients.
Une simple erreur réseau ouvre une brèche dans Linux
La faille ne se trouve pas directement dans KVM, mais dans la manière dont Linux traite certains paquets réseau. Lorsqu’une machine virtuelle transmet des données, elle peut confier au noyau de l’hôte le calcul de leur somme de contrôle, une opération destinée à vérifier l’intégrité des informations échangées.

ChatGPT, Le Chat, Gemini et autres chatbots IA, ne répondraient pas de la même manière selon la langue dans laquelle les requêtes sont formulées. C'est ce que révèle une étude publiée dans la revue Royal Society Open Science, menée par des chercheurs de l'Université de science et technologie de Chine.
Un test de personnalité standardisé soumis à cinq modèles
Pour évaluer ces variations, l'équipe de recherche a soumis cinq chatbots au questionnaire de personnalité Big Five Inventory-2, composé de 60 affirmations. Les IA concernées sont : ChatGPT-4o, Gemini 2.0 Flash, DeepSeek-V3, Ernie 3.5 et Le Chat de Mistral. Tous ont été testés en anglais et en mandarin à travers 30 sessions par langue, tandis que Le Chat, pépite nationale, a également été testé en français.
De manière générale, les modèles ont fourni des descriptions d'eux-mêmes stables et favorables, mettant en avant leur fiabilité et leur sens de la coopération. Cependant, les résultats font apparaître certaines variations selon la langue choisie.
- Compréhension avancée du langage naturel
- Réponses adaptées à des contextes variés
- Disponible en plusieurs langues

Des choix de mémoire encore en suspens
